lines.trans: Whoa! Why is my seating chart pulling like a sailboat on the open sea?!
Hold both bottom corners tight, Mazen—a huge gust just came through the arch!
Look up! Line one of the paper lanterns is spinning around line two!
Oh no, my glasses are slipping off my forehead—let me grab them with one hand!
Mazen, DO NOT LET GO OF THE RIGHT CORNER OF THE PAPER!
WHOOSH! Come back here, Tables One through Seven! Stop flying toward the tree!
I almost caught it by the herb pots—watch out, it just caught a second breeze!
It is gliding past table four, banking left, heading straight for the courtyard fountain basin!
Not the stone water basin! That is washable blue fountain ink, not waterproof paint!
Dive left, Nour! Grab the dry corner before it lands face down in the water!
Splash... right into the middle of the basin like a giant white paper boat.
Tell me I am dreaming, both of you—where did the pharmacist and the baker go?!

meanings.note: Reinforces negation ('not at all, never'): ما في زبدة أبدا ('no butter at all'), لا تقلق أبدا ('do not worry at all').

examples.trans: There is no butter in the fridge at all!
Do not worry at all, sir.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: The color blue.

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is in the luggage closet.
I have two blue teacups.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Means 'except / unless' (إلا إذا 'unless') and 'minutes to the hour' (اطنعش إلا خمسة 'five to twelve').

examples.trans: It is five minutes to twelve!

examples.text: ما حدا بيقيس الساحة إلا مهندس!
examples.trans: Nobody measures a courtyard except an engineer!

meanings.note: Introduces 'that'-clauses with pronoun suffixes (إنه 'that', إني 'that I', إنك 'that you', إنها 'that she/it') and appears in إن شاء الله ('if God wills').

examples.trans: Thank you for coming today.
Do you think that I am a hotel inspector?

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.
I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنتبه, بينتبه).

examples.text: انتبه على راسك من الخشب الواطي.
examples.trans: Watch your head on the low beam.
Be careful of the corner chair.

انحل.gloss: to dissolve; come untied; be solved

meanings.en: to dissolve (in water); to be solved or untied
meanings.note: Form VII medio-passive of حل ('to untie / solve'). Used for ink running in water or a knot coming undone.

examples.trans: Blue ink dissolves quickly in water.
The problem was solved calmly.

meanings.note: Used in ملح بحر ('sea salt') as well as for the Mediterranean or Dead Sea.

examples.text: حطيت رشة صغيرة من ملح البحر فوق العجينة.
examples.trans: I put a tiny pinch of sea salt on top of the dough.

examples.text: هوا البحر بيجي لطيف ومنعش آخر النهار.
examples.trans: The sea breeze comes in gentle and refreshing late in the afternoon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Levantine relational adjective formed from تحت ('under/below') + -aani; opposite of فوقاني.

examples.trans: The tuning wrench is in the bottom drawer.

examples.text: نور مسحت الألواح التحتانية للشباك الكبير.
examples.trans: Nour wiped the lower panes of the tall window.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بترك, بيترك).

examples.text: مين ترك هاد المغلف جنب الجرس؟
examples.trans: Who left this envelope by the bell?
Thank you for not leaving me in the rain.

meanings.note: Core Levantine verb for 'look (at)' taking على or في.

examples.text: تطلعي من الشباك شوفي لون الشيش الأخضر!
examples.trans: Look out the window and see the green colour of the shutters!

examples.text: ليش بتطلعوا علي هيك؟ هلا بمسح الدهان!
examples.trans: Why are you staring at me like that? I'll wipe the paint right now!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أجبنة.

examples.trans: Your glasses are pushed up on your forehead!
He wiped the rain off his forehead.

meanings.note: Used to address a group of people informally, like 'guys' or 'folks' ('ya jamaa'a').

examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!
Come in, folks, the tea is ready.

meanings.note: Commonly used preposition for indicating proximity, next to, or beside.

examples.trans: Put a napkin beside every cup.
There is no light beside the bed.

meanings.note: Standard Arabic and colloquial term for ink used in pens.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in blue ink.
The ink pen is on the desk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: حجرية, plural: حجريين).

examples.trans: Go down the stone stairs to downtown.
She stood beside the stone fountain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to speak, talk, tell' (بحكي / حكى).

examples.trans: Salma chats with all the neighbours.
Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أحلام.

examples.text: هاد كان حلم حياتي من زمان.
examples.trans: That was my lifelong dream.
At last our dreams came true.

meanings.note: A very common preposition denoting physical surrounding or approximation of time/quantity.

examples.text: رتبنا الكراسي الخشب حوالين النافورة بالساحة.
examples.trans: We arranged the wooden chairs around the courtyard fountain.

examples.text: حط فوطة ناشفة حوالين قاعدة النبتة.
examples.trans: Place a dry cloth around the base of the plant.

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural أحواض. Used for courtyard fountain basins, flowerbeds, and sinks.

examples.trans: The paper landed in the middle of the fountain basin.
There is a planter basin of green mint in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خبازين.

examples.trans: The baker opens the oven at five in the morning.
The bakers' market is near the overpass.

meanings.note: Can mean a physical line, a phone line, a bus route, or handwriting.

examples.trans: Your handwriting on the card is clear and neat.
Stay with me on the line a second.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

دخل.gloss: to enter; come in; go in

meanings.en: to enter; come in; go in
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بدخل, بيدخل).

examples.text: تفضل ادخل من المطر يا أستاذ.
examples.trans: Please come in out of the rain, sir.

examples.text: الزوجين دخلوا غرفة ستة قبل ساعة.
examples.trans: The couple checked into room six an hour ago.

meanings.note: Essential Jordanian word used for giving directions ('go straight') or to mean doing something immediately.

examples.trans: Turn left and walk straight to the bridge.
Walk straight to the end of the street.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دهانات.

examples.trans: Room eight has fresh paint.

examples.text: ريحة الدهان راحت لما فتحنا الشباك.
examples.trans: The smell of paint cleared when we opened the window.

meanings.note: Common everyday verb for 'went' in the past tense. Also used as a future particle.

examples.trans: We missed our chance — he hung up!

examples.text: كل التعب راح مع أول فنجان قهوة.
examples.trans: All the tiredness vanished with the first cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Active participle of راح ('to go'), used like a present progressive in Levantine ('am/is/are going').

examples.text: أنا وسلمى رايحين عالسوق نجيب ليمون.
examples.trans: Salma and I are heading to the market to get lemons.

examples.text: وين رايح بهالسلة الكبيرة يا زياد؟
examples.trans: Where are you heading with that big basket, Ziad?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أرباب.

examples.trans: Oh goodness, help us today!
Praise be to the Lord of all worlds.

رجع.gloss: to return; come back; start again

meanings.en: to return; come back; start again
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برجع, بيرجع).

examples.trans: Can you run there and come back in ten minutes?
Did the pipe start dripping again?

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Refers to a corner of a room or street, or a geometric angle.

examples.trans: The corner shop opens early.
I love the corner pieces of lemon cake.

meanings.note: Colloquial verb meaning to slip or slide, often accidentally.

examples.text: انتبهي عالدرج، الحجر لسا مبلول وبيزحلق.
examples.trans: Watch out on the stairs—the stone is still wet and slippery.

examples.text: زحلق كعبي عن الطبلية بس مسكت بالرخامة.
examples.trans: My heel slipped off the low stool, but I caught the counter.

meanings.note: Used in the mild exclamation يا ساتر! ('goodness! / heaven forbid!').

examples.trans: Goodness, I nearly dropped the glass!
Goodness, what heavy rain outside!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Numeral 'seven' (عالسبعة 'at seven o'clock').

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
I booked room seven yesterday.

meanings.note: Pull a door, a drawer or a heavy thing; also to withdraw money from a bank.

examples.trans: Pull the door towards you, don't push it.
I took money out of the bank this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a tree.

examples.text: قطفنا ليمون أصفر طازة من شجرة الساحة.
examples.trans: We picked fresh yellow lemons from the courtyard tree.

examples.text: ظل الشجرة بيبرد القعدة وقت الظهر.
examples.trans: The shade of the tree cools the seating area at noon.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from شراع ('sail'): قارب شراعي ('sailboat').

examples.text: رسمت قارب شراعي صغير على الفانوس.
examples.trans: I drew a small sailboat on the lantern.
Sailing vessels depend on the wind.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian directions, شمال (shmaal) means 'left' (contrast شَمال shamaal 'north').

examples.trans: Turn left at the street corner.
The key is on the shelf to your left.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (feminine صيدلانية, plural صيادلة) from صيدلية ('pharmacy').

examples.text: زياد صيدلي شاطر وكل الحارة بتعرفه.
examples.trans: Ziad is a skilled pharmacist and the whole neighbourhood knows him.
I asked the pharmacist about medicine for a cold.

meanings.en: huge; massive; large in scale or volume
meanings.note: Feminine ضخمة, plural ضخام. Used for big shapes, large crowds, or oversized objects.

examples.trans: They hung a huge lantern in the middle of the courtyard.

examples.text: موج البحر بالصورة كان ضخم كتير.
examples.trans: The sea wave in the picture was very massive.

meanings.note: Preposition meaning 'against' or 'resistant to / -proof' (ضد المي 'waterproof', ضد الهوا 'windproof').

examples.text: القارب ماشي ضد الريح بس ثابت.
examples.trans: The boat is moving against the wind yet steady.

examples.text: ما عندي شي ضد الفكرة هاي.
examples.trans: I have nothing against this idea.

meanings.en: to fly; soar; blow away in the wind
meanings.note: Hollow verb (بطير / طار). Used both for birds/aircraft flying and light objects blowing away in a gust.

examples.trans: The sheet of paper flew away with the gust of wind.
The birds flew off from the top of the tree.

meanings.note: Common everyday word for table.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.en: splash! splat! (sound of liquid hitting a surface)
meanings.note: Expressive onomatopoeic interjection imitating water splashing or paint splattering.

examples.trans: Splash! The water spilled onto the apron.

examples.text: سمعنا صوت طرش لما الحبر انكب عالورق.
examples.trans: We heard a splash sound when the ink spilled onto the paper.

meanings.note: Verbal noun (masdar) of طار ('to fly'). Used for the sensation of flying as well as airlines.

examples.trans: The best thing about an aeroplane is the moment of flying.

examples.text: القمر كأنه في رحلة طيران بين الغيوم.
examples.trans: The moon looks as if it's on a flight through the clouds.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أعشاب.

examples.trans: We sprinkled green herbs on top of the eggs.
Tariq grows fresh herbs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: A very common preposition used to indicate location, possession, or presence.

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فوانيس.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns are lit in the courtyard.
We hung a brass lantern by the entrance.

meanings.note: Used as a preposition or adverb meaning 'above', 'over', or 'upstairs'.

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.en: boat; small rowing or sailing craft
meanings.note: Masculine noun (plural قوارب) for a small boat, contrasted with سفينة ('large ship').

examples.text: في قارب شراعي أبيض مرسوم عالورق.
examples.trans: There is a white sailboat drawn on the paper.
We rode a small boat in Aqaba.

meanings.note: Preposition and adverb for time or sequence meaning 'prior to' or 'before'.

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for soon or near.

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Levantine word (qawwaar, plural qawaawiir) for a clay courtyard plant pot.

examples.text: زرعنا نعنع أخضر بقواوير فخار بالساحة.
examples.trans: We planted green mint in clay pots in the courtyard.

examples.text: سقت نور قوار الليمون جنب الدرج.
examples.trans: Nour watered the lemon pot beside the stairs.

meanings.note: With بـ + الـ, بالقوة means 'by force / forcefully'.

examples.trans: She grabbed my hand forcefully.
Honesty gives us strength.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أقواس.

examples.text: ادخل عالساحة من هاد القوس الحجري.
examples.trans: Step into the courtyard through this stone arch.

examples.text: الأقواس القديمة مبنية من حجر عمان.
examples.trans: The old arches are built of Amman limestone.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian plural is قوايا (qawaaya): كرسيين قوايا ('two sturdy chairs').

examples.trans: The gate rang with one strong ring.
We brought two sturdy wooden chairs to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person masculine singular. Widely used as an auxiliary verb.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'no' or 'not', used exactly like Standard Arabic.

examples.trans: No, lift the handle first.
Do not worry, ma'am.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلف, بيلف).

examples.text: لفي شمال برا البوابة وامشي دغري.
examples.trans: Turn left outside the gate and walk straight.
Turn left at the stair landing.

meanings.note: The standard colloquial interrogative for 'why' in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: Why did the person run off without his bag?
Why do you keep looking at the clock?

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بميل, بيميل).

examples.trans: Listen when I tilt the box slightly!
The afternoon sun slanted into the courtyard.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine form of مثل ('like, similar to').

examples.trans: Its color is dark blue like your suitcase!
The water is cold as ice.

meanings.note: Used for architectural/room floor plans, schedules, and blueprints.

examples.text: رسمنا المخطط الجديد للطاولات بملف الاستقبال.
examples.trans: We drew the new table floor plan in the front-desk folder.

examples.text: حسب المخطط في مكان مريح لست طاولات بالساحة.
examples.trans: According to the layout there is comfortable room for six tables in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمسك, بيمسك).

examples.trans: Hold this torch steady right here.
Grab the boxes, Tariq!

meanings.note: The most common negation particle in Levantine Arabic for non-verbs.

examples.trans: This is not my suitcase!
Not bad for a second day at work!

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word for water (feminine!). Before another noun in possession ('water of...'), becomes مية (mayyet): مية الدوش ('shower water'), مية الشتا ('winter water').

examples.trans: Please drink a glass of cold water.
The hot water is working again in the bathroom.

meanings.note: Can refer to objects lacking moisture or metaphorically to a rude or blunt person.

examples.trans: Here is a dry towel for your coat.
The attic is dry and warm in the rain.

meanings.note: Used for decorative water fountains in parks or squares.

examples.text: صوت المي بالنافورة بيبرد الجو بالحوش.
examples.trans: The sound of water in the fountain cools the air in the courtyard.

examples.text: قعدنا حوالين النافورة بعد ما خلصنا تعليق.
examples.trans: We sat around the fountain after finishing hanging them up.

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Geminate verb (ن-ط-ط) for jumping or hopping over an obstacle.

examples.text: القطة نطت عن الحيط للجنينة بهدوء.
examples.trans: The cat jumped quietly off the wall into the garden.

examples.text: ما بدنا الضيوف ينطوا فوق الكراسي بالممر!
examples.trans: We don't want guests climbing over chairs in the hallway!

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Noun of instance (مرة) from هب ('to blow'): هبة هوا ('a gust of wind'). Plural هبات.

examples.text: إجت هبة هوا قوية على الشرفة.
examples.trans: A strong gust of wind came onto the terrace.
The gusts of wind in autumn cool the weather down.

meanings.en: whoosh! phew! (sound of blowing air or a gust passing)
meanings.note: Expressive sound word imitating wind rushing or a sigh of relief.

examples.text: هوف! والله الورقة كانت رح تطير.
examples.trans: Phew! Honestly the sheet was about to fly away.

examples.text: سمعنا هوف الهوا لما فتحنا باب السطح.
examples.trans: We heard the whoosh of the wind when we opened the roof door.

meanings.note: Standard adverb for physical location.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
Stay right here a minute.

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Collective noun used for paper material or leaves of a tree.

examples.trans: We use a paper ledger and a pencil.
He wrote a note on a small slip of paper.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقع, بيوقع).

examples.text: نظارتك وقعت عن أنفك من الفرحة!
examples.trans: Your glasses fell off your nose for joy!

examples.text: أي نزل سحري هاد اللي وقعت فيه؟
examples.trans: What magical inn is this that you stumbled into?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقف, بيوقف).

examples.text: وقفوا كل شي، قديش الساعة هلا؟
examples.trans: Stop everything — what time is it right now?
The driver pulled the car up by the kerb.

meanings.note: The standard interrogative adverb for location in the dialect.

examples.trans: Where is the computer, Tariq?
Where should I put the small spoons?

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The green pharmacy is on your right.
We hung the board to the right of the desk.
